Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €11839 spend · 226 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Multi-product formats dominate: 'Carousel_120237873305580396 - Copy' leads at 3.34x ROAS with the lowest CPP in the account (€27.75), and 'Static _ Catalog #2' delivers 2.36x ROAS at €35.34 CPP—showing more products per ad clearly converts Belgian shoppers.
• Product-specific statics win big: 'Static _ Tennis #2' is the account MVP at 6.36x ROAS and €23.54 CPP but criminally underspent at €71. 'Static _ Summer #2' combines volume (41 purchases) with 2.55x ROAS—the best scaled performer.
• Product-focused video quietly works: 'Video _ General #3' hits 3.28x ROAS at €35 CPP, proving short product showcases convert where lifestyle content fails.
❌ What's Not Working
• Split concept is bleeding cash: 'Static _ Split #1' burned €1,225 at 0.9x ROAS, and 'Static _ Split #2' only manages 1.97x at €55 CPP—the entire concept underperforms in Belgium.
• Lifestyle and branded video is a money pit: 'Video _ Organic #1' wasted €512 at 0.8x ROAS and 'Video _ Tagline #2' is the account's worst performer at 0.47x—brand storytelling doesn't sell here.
• Heart concept is wildly inconsistent: 'Static _ Heart Split #1' (€123 CPP) and 'Static _ Heart Tag #1' (€148 CPP) are catastrophic, while only 'Static _ Heart White #1' (2.25x) proves the product can work with the right creative.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carousel and catalog multi-product layouts: replicate the Carousel and Catalog #2 format across every product category (Tennis, Summer, Heart). This format owns the best CPP and ROAS combo in Belgium.
• Tennis collection statics: 'Static _ Tennis #2' at 6.36x ROAS is screaming for more variants and serious budget. Build 3-4 new Tennis statics immediately.
• Short, product-focused video in the style of 'Video _ General #3': quick cuts, close-ups on jewelry, no lifestyle fluff. This is the only video format that converts—make more of it.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All Split creatives: both variants underperform. The layout/concept doesn't resonate in Belgium—stop testing it.
• 'Video _ Organic #1' and 'Video _ Tagline #2': lifestyle and branding video is burning budget with sub-1x ROAS. Pause both immediately and redirect spend to product-focused formats.
• Every Heart variant except 'Heart White #1' and 'Heart Tag #2': Heart Split, Heart Catalog, and Heart Tag #1 have CPPs from €58 to €148 with ROAS under 1.3x—they're dead weight dragging the account.

kleyo — Ads Report

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €6691 spend · 116 results
✅ What's Working
• Comparison format (Vergelijking #2) is the proven volume engine — 32 leads at €46.89 CPL at top spend, and three variants all convert, proving the broker-fee-savings angle is the sharpest hook for Belgian homeowners.
• Savings calculator (Berekening #2) delivers the best efficient static CPL at €40.02 across 15 leads — hard math showing exact euros saved converts better than abstract messaging.
• Thomas Guenter testimonial (€110 variant) is the cheapest lead source in the account at €22.03 CPL — real-person social proof massively outperforms polished creative when copy lands right.
❌ What's Not Working
• Vergelijking #1 is a money pit — both variants combined spent €367 for just 2 leads at ~€184 avg CPL, while Vergelijking #2 does the same job 3-4x cheaper. Whatever creative difference exists, #1 repels conversions.
• Poll #2 and Review #2 are engagement-bait formats failing at lead gen — €198 and €143 CPL respectively. High-consideration home-selling decisions don't respond to lightweight social formats.
• General Video #1 Copy variants collapse (€95-309 CPL) while the originals thrive at €28-31 CPL — the copy or audience layering on these duplicates is actively destroying a winning creative.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more savings-math statics in the Berekening mold — show exact euro savings at €300K, €400K, €500K+ price points. The calculator angle is your most efficient static format and has clear iteration potential.
• Mine real-seller testimonials aggressively — Thomas Guenter at €22 CPL proves social proof converts harder than anything else. Find 3-4 more happy sellers and build static + video variants.
• Refresh the Vergelijking #2 comparison format with new visual treatments before creative fatigue sets in — this is your highest-volume proven concept and you already have 3+ variants running.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Vergelijking #1 variants immediately — €367 across two copies for 2 total leads. The #2 version does the same job at a quarter of the cost. No iteration will save this.
• Kill Poll #2 — €397 for 2 leads at €198 CPL. Polls are awareness candy, not lead-gen tools for €200K+ selling decisions.
• Kill General Video #1 Copy (€309 variant) and Thomas Guenter Copy 2 (€138, zero leads) — both are broken duplicates of winning originals, bleeding budget for nothing.

Creative Analysis

10 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

10 ads · €1147 spend · 12 purchases
✅ What's Working
• USvThem comparison format is the clear winner — "Static _ USvThem #1" delivered 28.1x ROAS at €22 CPP, proving competitive positioning resonates hard with Belgian coffee buyers.
• Social proof creatives have untapped scale potential — "Static _ Review #1" (15.23x ROAS) and "Static _ Review #2" (5.45x ROAS) both convert in the right audience, but have been starved of budget at €13 and €37 respectively.
• High CTRs across the board (90-160%+) confirm the brand captures attention — the bottleneck is converting clicks to purchases, not generating interest.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Search #1" is a money pit — €271 combined spend across both instances, only 2 purchases at best, 0.56x ROAS. Search-style creative does not translate to social feeds.
• "Static _ Chat #1" is a clickbait trap — highest CTRs in the account (149-161%) but zero purchases across both instances. People engage out of curiosity but have no buying intent.
• The high-spend instance of "Static _ Review #2" (€357, 0.67x ROAS) is bleeding cash while the same creative at €37 delivers 5.45x — the audience or placement at scale is fundamentally wrong.
⬆ Double Down On
• USvThem comparison creatives — produce 2-3 new variants with different angles (supermarket beans, capsule pods, generic online retailers). The format is proven at 28.1x ROAS.
• Review and social proof statics — build a full suite with different customer quotes, blend-specific testimonials, and star ratings. "Static _ Review #1" at 15.23x has barely been tested.
• Expertise-led positioning — lean into "we test every machine on the market" as a trust signal. This USP is completely untapped in current creative and naturally extends the USvThem format that's already winning.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All "Static _ Search #1" variants — pull budget immediately. The format does not work for this brand on Meta, period.
• Both "Static _ Chat #1" instances — high CTR with zero conversions is the clearest signal of wasted spend. The curiosity hook attracts browsers, not buyers.
• The high-spend "Static _ Review #2" instance at €357 — the creative works (proven at €37 with 5.45x), but whatever targeting is behind the €357 version is broken. Kill it and reallocate.

Creative Analysis

🇧🇪

Belgium

12 ads · €1061 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Exceptionally high CTRs across all angles — 'Static _ Myth #2' (134.82%), 'Static _ General #1' (125.57%), and 'Static _ General #2' (111.80%) prove the creative hooks are grabbing attention in Belgium.
• Three distinct messaging angles (USvsTHEM, Myth, General) are all generating clicks — no single angle is failing to drive engagement, suggesting strong creative variety.
• Static format is clearly resonating with this audience — every ad is pulling meaningful click volume relative to spend.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions across ALL 12 ads and €1,061 total spend — this is not a creative problem, this is a broken funnel. Tracking, landing page, or conversion event is misconfigured.
• High CTRs (many exceeding 100%) with 0 results strongly indicates either the pixel isn't firing, the landing page is broken/misaligned, or the wrong conversion event is selected in campaign setup.
• Duplicate ad names running simultaneously ('Static _ USvsTHEM #2', 'Static _ Myth #1', etc.) with wildly different CTRs suggest fragmented testing with no clean read — muddying any learnable signal.
⬆ Double Down On
• FIX THE FUNNEL FIRST — do not spend another euro until conversion tracking is verified end-to-end (pixel, CAPI, thank-you page event). Every creative insight is meaningless until this is resolved.
• Once fixed, prioritize Myth-busting and General angles — they consistently pull the highest CTRs (92-134%) and likely resonate with Belgian homeowners debunking EV charging misconceptions.
• Create Belgium-specific landing pages in Dutch/French with localized social proof, Belgian installation imagery, and clear CTA — generic NL pages likely kill conversion for BE traffic.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop all spend immediately — €1,061 burned with zero results is unacceptable. Not one ad has delivered a single conversion.
• Kill the duplicate ad structure — running identical creatives ('Static _ Myth #1' x2, 'Static _ USvsTHEM #2' x2, etc.) across overlapping audiences cannibalizes delivery and wastes budget.
• Stop launching new creatives until the post-click experience is audited and confirmed converting.

Belgium

2 ads · €336 spend · 19 results
✅ What's Working
• Investment angle is pulling leads — "Static _ Investeren _ 2" delivering 19 results at €17.58 CPR, which is strong for real estate lead gen in Belgium.
• Static format with investment messaging clearly resonates with the Belgian audience seeking Zeeland property opportunities.
• The "Investeren" positioning validates that the financial/rental-guarantee angle cuts through — lean into this.
❌ What's Not Working
• Extreme creative underinvestment — only 2 ads running in this entire market means zero learnings on angles, formats, or audiences.
• "Static _ Investeren _ 3" has received virtually no spend (€2) and zero results — either throttled by Meta or losing the auction against its sibling ad.
• No lifestyle, second-home, or emotional creative exists — the entire funnel is one-note investment messaging with no top-of-funnel dream-building.
⬆ Double Down On
• Investment-angle statics with sharper financial hooks (100% verhuurgarantie, rendement aan het water) — proven winner, needs variants.
• Introduce video and carousel formats to the investment narrative — the static is working, now test richer storytelling around the same theme.
• Launch a parallel lifestyle track — Westerschelde panoramas, rust-en-ruimte imagery, weekend-aan-het-water aspiration — to open a second lead pipeline beyond pure investors.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running only 2 ads — this is a real estate project with multiple USPs and you're betting everything on one creative.
• Kill the assumption that investment is the only angle worth running — second home and primary residence buyers are untapped.

Netherlands

5 ads · €581 spend · 16 results
✅ What's Working
• "Video _ Lifestyle #1" is the standout — €13.13 CPR at highest CTR (523%) proves emotional, cinematic water-lifestyle storytelling converts Dutch leads cheaply.
• "Static _ Water Wind _ Form" delivers volume (9 leads at €36.1) — nature/space/water imagery with a direct form CTA is a reliable lead engine.
• Video format dramatically outperforms static across the board — lifestyle aspiration beats rational investment messaging in this market.
❌ What's Not Working
• The entire "Investeren" static series is underperforming or dead — "Static _ Investeren _ 2 - Copy" burned €177 for only 2 leads at €88.34 CPR, and the other two variants got zero results on minimal spend. Rational investment messaging falls flat.
• Static-heavy creative mix is limiting scale — 4 of 5 ads are static, yet the single video crushes all of them on efficiency.
• Copy-variant testing on a losing concept (Investeren copies) wastes budget instead of exploring new creative directions.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more cinematic lifestyle video content — water, light, panoramic Westerschelde views, rust-and-space vibes. The emotional pull is what converts.
• Lean into the "Water Wind" nature/space territory with fresh angles — sunrise drone shots, seasonal moods, tidal rhythms. This static concept proved it works; video versions could 3x it.
• Create kijkwoning visit-focused content — walkthrough video, before/after lifestyle narrative — to convert the high intent this audience clearly has.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running "Investeren" static variants — the investment-rational angle is a dead end in this market at current creative quality. Three variants, combined €191 spent, 2 total leads.
• Stop duplicating losing concepts with "Copy" variants — iterate on winners instead.

Other

23 ads · €5102 spend · 153 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Water Wind _ Form" is the runaway winner — 56 leads at €8.84 each. Evocative water/wind lifestyle + embedded form is the formula.
• Product-specific ads crush generic lifestyle: "Static _ Nieuw_App #1" (€7.34/lead) and "Static _ Video #2" (€8.85/lead) deliver sub-€10 leads with minimal spend — begging to be scaled.
• Highest CTRs correlate with top performers (Video #2 at 670%, Nieuw_App #1 at 666%) — visual specificity and new-product framing drive both clicks and conversions.
❌ What's Not Working
• The "Dreamer" concept is a money pit: Dreamer #1 at €54.52/lead, Dreamer #2 at €108.94/lead, and the second Dreamer #2 variant burned €41 with zero results. Dreamy ≠ converting.
• "Static _ Review _ Form" is the highest spender (€1,278) yet delivers leads at €75.19 each — social proof framing isn't landing at this price point.
• Investment-focused ads are failing: "Investeren _ 3 - Copy 2" burned €263 with zero leads; the investment angle lacks specificity or urgency.
⬆ Double Down On
• Water + Form formula: Create more variants pairing atmospheric Westerschelde visuals with embedded lead forms — this is your €8.84 CPL goldmine.
• New product announcements: The "Nieuw_App" angle at €7.34/lead proves scarcity/newness hooks outperform generic lifestyle. Launch fresh variants for houses and hotel apartments.
• Short-form video content: "Static _ Video #2" matches Water Wind's CPL at €8.85 with the highest CTR in the account (670%). Video is undertested and clearly working — triple down here.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Dreamer variants immediately — €532 spent across three ads with 7 leads at €76/avg. The vague aspirational tone doesn't convert for a €200K+ real estate decision.
• Kill "Static _ Investeren _ 3 - Copy 2" — €263 and zero leads. Generic investment messaging without rental guarantee specifics is wasted budget.
• Kill "Static _ Review _ Form" — €1,278 for 17 leads at €75.19 is 8.5x worse than your best performer. Reallocate immediately.

🇧🇪

Belgium

21 ads · €1190 spend · 132 results
✅ What's Working
• Naoshima #2 is the clear champion: 43 leads at €5.81 each — best efficiency at scale. The minimalist Japanese-architectural aesthetic clearly resonates with this affluent audience.
• Sommerfeld #3 and Bauhaus #2 are reliable workhorses: 28 and 39 results respectively at sub-€10 CPR. Together with Naoshima #2, these three originals account for 85% of all leads.
• Sommerfeld #2 shows a hidden gem signal: €6.41 CPR across 6 results on just €38 spend — starved of budget but highly efficient.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single 'Copy' variant underperforms its original — Sommerfeld #1-Copy is catastrophic at €62.91/lead, Sommerfeld #2-Copy 5x worse than its original, Bauhaus #2-Copy spent €17 with zero results. The duplication strategy (likely different ad sets or audiences) is bleeding budget.
• Bauhaus #5 (€14.52 CPR), Bauhaus #3-Copy (€17.33), and Bauhaus #6-Copy (€19.37) are 2-3x the cost of top performers — mediocre creatives propped up by spend.
• No ROAS tracking on any ad. For luxury real estate at €500K+ price points, flying blind on revenue attribution is a critical gap.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Naoshima-style minimalist architectural visuals — clean lines, light, restraint. This aesthetic outperforms the busier Bauhaus and Sommerfeld angles on both CPR and volume.
• Consolidate budget into proven originals (Naoshima #2, Sommerfeld #2, #3, Bauhaus #2) and kill the Copy fragmentation. Fewer ad sets, more signal, faster optimization.
• Introduce video and carousel formats — the static-only creative mix is untested against richer formats that can showcase architectural walkthroughs, details, and coastal context for this high-consideration purchase.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all 'Copy' variants immediately — they've collectively spent €235 for 8 leads at €29.38 avg CPR vs €855 for 110 leads at €7.77 avg CPR for originals. The audience or placement split is destroying performance.
• Stop spreading €1-€6 across 8+ low-spend Bauhaus variants. Meta can't optimize with dust budgets — consolidate into 3-4 proven Bauhaus creatives max.
• Stop running lead-gen without ROAS tracking. Connect CRM data to Meta — one Rietveld sale likely covers the entire annual ad budget.

28 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

28 ads · €1684 spend · 51 results
✅ What's Working
• B2B creative is the entire engine — all 51 results come from B2B ads. "Static _ B2B _ 4 Momenten #1" (€18.13 CPR) and "Static _ B2B _ Boost #2" (€21.81 CPR, 16 results) are clear winners with strong engagement and efficient cost per result.
• Use-case-specific B2B angles (coffee bars, brunch menus, speed of prep) resonate hard — "Static _ B2B _ Upgrade Brunch" and "Static _ B2B _ Açai Koffiebar" both convert despite modest budgets.
• Practical, benefit-driven B2B hooks ('4 momenten', 'boost', 'snel') outperform abstract or clever concepts like 'geen excuus' or 'this is how we bowl'.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single B2C ad has zero results — €321 in total wasted across Notes, Deinze, Watersportbaan, Carrousel, Organic, Wekker, and Craving creatives. The B2C static strategy is fundamentally broken.
• Location-based B2C ads ("Static _ Deinze #1", "Static _ Watersportbaan #1") generate almost no engagement (CTR 2-3%) and zero conversions — hyper-local static creative without a clear CTA or retail tie-in doesn't work.
• "Static _ B2B _ Geen excuus #1" burned €89 for a single result (€89.04 CPR) — the 'no excuses' angle generates high curiosity clicks but doesn't convert to action.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more B2B variations around the winning hooks: time-saving (Snel), menu revenue uplift (Boost/Menukaart), and daypart occasions (4 Momenten). These are proven conversion themes.
• Develop a proper B2C creative strategy from scratch — the current statics are not converting. Prioritize video/UGC formats with explicit retail CTAs pointing to Bio-Planet and Delhaize, leveraging endorsers (Bekkari, Binge, Gruyaert) who are completely absent from current ads.
• Create B2B video content — if static B2B already converts at €18-22 CPR, short-form video showing real café prep or a quick testimonial should compress costs further and unlock scale.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all B2C static ads immediately — zero results across 10 creatives is not a sample-size problem, it's a format/message problem. Stop bleeding €300+/month on this.
• Pause "Static _ B2B _ Geen excuus #1" — €89 per result is 4-5x worse than your best B2B ads. The hook is too vague for B2B decision-makers.
• Stop running location-specific ads (Deinze, Watersportbaan) without store-finder CTAs or retail partner branding — they read as generic brand posts, not performance ads.

⬆ Double Down On

• Product-focused creatives that bridge browsing to buying — mimic the structure of the 4.03x ROAS winner.
• Test more volume at the €44-45 CPP sweet spot — the two profitable ads prove the unit economics can work, now scale the winning formula.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running vague emoji-only or copy-less ads — they generate clicks but zero revenue. "❤️" and """" are vanity metrics traps.
• Stop treating all "Instagram Post" creatives equally — one is at 0.89x ROAS while another is at 2.34x. Differentiate and cut the loser.

✅ What's Working
• Both ads (120239394435940631 and 120239393986810631) generate extreme click-through rates (122%+ and 161%+), meaning the creative hooks are grabbing attention — people are clearly interested in workwear content.
• Low combined spend (€89) means the brand hasn't burned significant budget yet while learning. The audience is clearly responsive to workwear messaging in Belgium.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions across both ads despite strong CTRs — this screams broken conversion tracking or a campaign objective set to traffic/engagement instead of conversions. Clicks mean nothing without results.
• €89 spent with literally nothing to show for it. 120239394435940631 at €59 and 120239393986810631 at €30 are both pure waste until the funnel is fixed.
• Likely no pixel, CAPI, or proper conversion event firing on the landing page. High CTR + zero results is the textbook symptom.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix tracking infrastructure FIRST — install Meta Pixel + Conversions API, verify purchase/lead events fire correctly, then relaunch.
• Lean into the high-engagement creative style that's clearly resonating — whatever visual/copy approach is driving those clicks, it works for attention.
• Build a B2B-specific funnel: workwear catalog request, quote request, or bulk order form — give those clickers somewhere meaningful to convert.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running any conversion-optimized campaigns until tracking is confirmed working end-to-end. Every euro is wasted right now.
• Kill the assumption that clicks equal success — 0 results at any CTR is failure.

🛑 Kill or Rethink

Other

30 ads · €9637 spend · 132 results
✅ What's Working
• Native format is the clear winner — "stokerie_int_native" (22 results, €49.83 CPR) and "stokerie_int_v1_rem - native" (10 results, €31.04 CPR) both crush it with sky-high CTRs.
• Animation beats video hands down at Vottem — "Vottem_animatie" delivers €25.51 CPR vs €55.59 for "Vottem_video" and €80.70 for "Vottem_logements". Nearly 3x more efficient.
• Terrain/exterior lifestyle content for Awans converts cheaply — "awans_terrain_v1" at €26.42 CPR with 9 results from only €238 spend is the portfolio's hidden gem.
❌ What's Not Working
• Wildebeek is a money pit across every creative variant — "wildebeek_realisatie_video" (€185.67 CPR), "wildebeek_drink - v2" (€177.48 CPR), "wildebeek_int" (0 results), "ODD Wildenbeek 1/10/26" (0 results). Four ads, €991 spent, 3 total results.
• Charleroi rental play is dead — "Charleroi_te-huur" burned €322 for zero results, and "Charleroi_native" at €129.19 CPR is 3-5x worse than top performers.
• Remarketing carousel and reel formats flop — "carousel_fr_rem" (€174, 0 results) and "Awans_reel" (€224, 0 results) prove format alone doesn't save weak creative.
⬆ Double Down On
• Scale native-format interior content — it's the consistent winner across projects. Replicate the Stokerie native playbook for Brugge, Vottem, and West.
• Lean hard into animation/3D walkthrough creative — Vottem_animatie's €25.51 CPR proves this format resonates for real estate. Apply it to every project with available 3D assets.
• Invest in terrain/lifestyle exterior shots à la "awans_terrain_v1" — location-forward content that sells the neighborhood, not just the unit, converts cheaply and builds pipeline.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Wildebeek ads immediately — the project has burned nearly €1K with catastrophic CPRs. Either the offer, audience, or creative is fundamentally broken. Diagnose before spending another euro.
• Pause "Charleroi_te-huur" and "west_kijkapt_native" — zero results and €354.75 CPR respectively. Pure waste.
• Stop running reels and carousels without a proven concept — "Awans_reel" and "carousel_fr_rem" both delivered nothing. Don't test format for format's sake.

Belgium

30 ads · €3853 spend · 90 results
✅ What's Working
• "Doorstromer" audience segment is the clear winner — "Static _ Doorstromer #1 - Copy" delivers €13.89/result at scale (40 results), and "Static _ Doorstromer #2 - Copy" hits €10.59/result, the lowest CPR in the account.
• "Alleenstaand" segment also converts efficiently — "Static _ Alleenstaand #2" pulls 24 results at €15.61 and "Static _ Alleenstaand #1" gets 2 results at €16.14, both well under the bloated CPRs elsewhere.
• Original (non-V2) creative variants consistently outperform their V2 counterparts on cost/result, suggesting the original messaging/visuals resonate better.
❌ What's Not Working
• V2 variants are burning cash — "Static _ Doorstromer V2 #1" ate €1,534 for only 10 results at a brutal €153.36/result, and "Static _ Alleenstaand #2 V2" spent €146 for 2 results at €73.16. The V2 refresh failed.
• "General/Algemeen" ads produce zero results across all variants (€387 total spend, 0 conversions). No audience resonance whatsoever.
• "Jong Koppel" and "ODD" segments are underspending with near-zero conversions — combined €245 spend, 1 total result. Either the targeting or the creative misses entirely.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more "Doorstromer" original-style creatives — this segment converts cheaply and scales. Test new angles, pain points, and formats for this audience.
• Expand "Alleenstaand" with fresh creative iterations following the original (non-V2) visual/copy style that's already proven at €13-16 CPR.
• Test video and carousel formats for the winning segments — every ad is static, leaving format diversification as a massive untapped lever.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all V2 variants immediately — they universally deliver worse CPR than originals while eating the majority of spend. The creative refresh backfired.
• Kill all "General/Algemeen" ads — €387 spent, zero results. Generic messaging doesn't convert for this brand.
• Kill "Jong Koppel V2" ads — €91 spent, zero results, no signal worth chasing.

✅ What's Working
• "VERANDAS PUB CONVERTION - Copie" is the only ad converting — €6.68/result is outstanding for a high-ticket veranda business. Veranda-specific messaging clearly resonates.
• Abnormally high CTRs across all ads (111-301%) suggest creative is grabbing attention and driving engagement — the click problem isn't creative, it's post-click.
• Conversion-optimized campaign structure ("PUB CONVERTION") on the veranda ad is generating leads where others fail.
❌ What's Not Working
• "CARPORTS" burned €42 with zero results — highest spend, worst outcome. Clicks flood in but nothing converts; landing page or offer is broken.
• "PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS" same story: €19, massive CTR, zero conversions. The post-click experience is leaking every lead.
• Total account spend is only €75/month — this budget is too thin to learn anything meaningful on 4 separate campaigns. Fragmentation is killing optimization.
⬆ Double Down On
• Veranda-specific creative — it's the only proven converter. Build more angles around veranda projects (seasonal, lifestyle, before/after).
• Fix the post-click funnel for carports and pergolas before spending another euro. The clicks prove demand exists; the zero conversions prove the landing page kills it.
• Consolidate budget behind what converts. Stop spreading €75 across four campaigns and feed the winner.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running carport and pergola ads until landing pages are rebuilt and tested — you're paying for clicks that go nowhere.
• Kill the habit of launching new campaigns at €1-€19 spend levels. That's not testing, that's guessing.

• Nothing is converting — zero results across the entire account.
• The 57.94% CTR on 'Static _ Veranda _ Lifestyle #1 - Copy' suggests the creative generates curiosity or engagement, but this metric is suspiciously high and likely inflated by misattribution, engagement bait, or micro-sample noise.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Static _ Veranda _ Lifestyle #1 - Copy' burned €68 with zero results — the pixel, conversion event, or landing page funnel is almost certainly broken. Fix tracking before spending another euro.
• Running a single ad copy (literally labeled '- Copy') from an unverified multi-account is a red flag — no creative diversity, no testing structure, no strategy.
⬆ Double Down On
• Verify tracking end-to-end before any new spend: pixel fires, conversion event mapping, landing page load, thank-you page trigger.
• Clarify what 'MULTI COMPTE' actually is — shared agency account, holding company, or rogue sub-account. Audit permissions and billing.
• If veranda/conservatory is the real product, build a proper creative testing framework from scratch with diverse angles and formats.

🌐

Other

29 ads · €5504 spend · 136 results
✅ What's Working
• Mixed product video format crushes it — "MIX VERANCOBEL - VIDEO - NEW 2026 - Copie" delivers the lowest CPR at €15.71 with 8 results on minimal spend. Video + brand bundling is the winning formula.
• Carports are the most consistent product line — four carport variants deliver between €17.49 and €46.40 CPR, with the lowest-spend variant (€105) actually producing the best efficiency at €17.49. This category converts reliably.
• "PUB PERGOLAS 3" and "Static _ Veranda _ Lifestyle #1 - Copy - Copie" both deliver sub-€25 CPR proving that simple, direct creatives outperform overproduced carousels for lead gen.
❌ What's Not Working
• PVC creatives are a money pit — "PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3" burned €107 for zero results and another €174 for only 2 results at €86.97 CPR. The PVC video format is fundamentally broken.
• Duplicate ad names with wildly different CPRs signal zero audience/placement control — "PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4" ranges from €22.56 to €80.02 CPR across four instances, and "VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - Copie" swings from €54.36 to €181.72. This screams audience overlap and cannibalization.
• The account structure itself is suspect — "MULTI COMPTE" naming, French "Copie" suffixes everywhere, and typos like "MUTLI" suggest no one is actively managing creative strategy. This is set-and-forget chaos.
⬆ Double Down On
• Scale the mixed-product video format — "MIX VERANCOBEL" proves bundling multiple products in one branded video drives the cheapest leads. Produce 3-4 new variants with seasonal angles, installation footage, and customer proof.
• Double down on carports as the lead product line — it's the most efficient and consistent category. Create new carport-specific creatives (before/after, material close-ups, pricing anchors) and give them more budget.
• Invest in lifestyle static imagery — "Static _ Veranda _ Lifestyle #1" at €23.04 CPR shows aspirational product-in-situ shots convert. Produce a full lifestyle photo suite across all product categories.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all PVC video ads immediately — both "PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3" variants are burning cash with near-zero returns. The format does not work for this product.
• Kill the worst "VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - Copie" (€181.72 CPR, 1 result) — this is the single worst ad in the account and should have been paused weeks ago.
• Kill the worst-performing "PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4" variant (€80.02 CPR, 2 results on €160 spend) — consolidate pergola budget into the winning variant at €22.56 CPR.

8 ads · €1031 spend · 93 results
✅ What's Working
• Static images dominate: "Schoonmaak - Zwin - image" delivers the best cost/result at €6.22 with strong engagement (411% CTR), proving simple visuals convert for public campaigns.
• "Visual | Wedstrijd" is the volume workhorse — 61 results on €689 spend at an acceptable €11.29 CPR, showing contest mechanics reliably drive public participation.
• "Video" (generic) hints at potential with a €2.16 CPR on tiny spend, suggesting short-form video can outperform when the concept is right.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Schoonmaak - Zwin - video" is a disaster — €45 spent for 1 result at €45.44 CPR while the identical campaign as a static image costs 7× less. Video added friction, not value.
• Complex formats flopped: "Carrousel | Wedstrijd" (€33.73 CPR) and "Gif | Wedstrijd" (zero results on €11) prove that carousel and gif formats are overcomplicating what should be simple public-sector messaging.
• Budget is heavily concentrated in "Visual | Wedstrijd" (63% of total spend) while the most efficient ad ("Schoonmaak - Zwin - image") is starved at €93.
⬆ Double Down On
• Static image creatives for civic campaigns — the image format consistently outperforms video, carousel, and gif across both campaign themes. Produce more single-image variants.
• Contest/wedstrijd mechanics with simple visuals — the combination of participation incentive + clean static creative is your most scalable formula.
• Environmental/nature themes like the Zwin cleanup — this topic drove the lowest CPR, suggesting strong civic resonance. Create more nature-preservation content.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill carousel and gif formats entirely for this account — neither delivered meaningful results and both inflated costs dramatically.
• Stop running video and image variants of the same campaign simultaneously without proper A/B structure — the Zwin split proves video cannibalizes budget without converting.

🌐

Other

11 ads · €422 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Nothing is converting — zero results across all 11 ads, €422 completely wasted on boosted posts with no conversion objective.
• High engagement signals on 'Je meest geliefde Marie Jo fit...' (1052% CTR) and 'Van harte welkom in onze nieuwe winkel in Lokeren' (830% CTR) suggest these creatives resonate emotionally, but engagement without conversion tracking is vanity.
• Brand storytelling around known lingerie labels (Marie Jo, PrimaDonna) and the new Lokeren store clearly sparks interest — the audience is there, the funnel is not.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single ad is a boosted organic post ('Bericht'/'Instagram-bericht') with no pixel-based conversion objective — this is why results are literally zero. The account has no performance infrastructure.
• Reels 'Sheary-Tom' (€13) and 'Juliane' (€9) are low-spend afterthoughts with no clear CTA or product focus — they get engagement but drive nothing.
• The impossibly high 'CTR' figures (300–1052%) confirm Meta is reporting all-clicks/engagement on boosted posts, not meaningful link clicks — the data is misleading and masks total failure.
⬆ Double Down On
• Rebuild from scratch: create proper conversion campaigns with Advantage+ or manual purchase/lead objectives, install and verify Meta Pixel + CAPI before spending another euro.
• The Marie Jo and PrimaDonna branded content gets eyeballs — repurpose those product stories into proper direct-response ads with clear CTAs, product pages, and retargeting.
• The Lokeren store opening content ('Van harte welkom...') shows strong local engagement — create a dedicated local awareness + store visit campaign with a real objective instead of boosting.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting organic posts immediately. Not a single boost has generated a tracked result. This is lighting money on fire for likes.
• Kill the spray-and-pray micro-budget approach (€9–€60 per ad). Consolidate budget into 2–3 properly structured campaigns with real objectives.
